cases.name: Cordelia Mae Guevara
cases.about: She operated a lounge called La Chiquita Fajita.
cases.narrative:
He stayed as the lounge she worked at was closing for the noght and stabbed her 14 times while sexually assaulting her.

Nueces County Medical Examiner Joseph C. Rupp went to the scene of the crime as well as performed her autopsy. Dr. Rupp related his observations. (She) "was on her back with her legs spread, her panties were not on the body, her clothing was torn, and, ... the ... legs were spread and flexed, the skirt was pulled up and torn." Tests performed during autopsy revealed a positive finding for prostatic acid phosphate in the deceased's vagina leaving "no doubt ... there was sexual activity involved in this crime."

Dr. Rupp found twelve distinct stab wounds. His findings observed "... the left lung was penetrated four times, the heart was penetrated once ... a major artery was also penetrated ... the heart was sort of penetrated twice ... and then the wound lower down here got the stomach."

cases.name: Mary Alice "Alicia" Anzaldua
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Alicia lived a life marked by dedication, kindness, and an unwavering commitment to her family and friends. Alicia was a woman of vibrant character, known for her outspoken nature and her ability to light up any room with her presence. She was a hardworking mother and sister who approached every challenge with determination and grace. Her love for her family was immense, and she instilled in them the values of love and selflessness that she embodied every day.

Her interests were simple yet brought her immense joy. Alicia had an affinity for yellow roses, which reflected her bright and cheerful spirit. She found pleasure in the excitement of scratch-off tickets and cherished the moments of relaxation with a cold Coca-Cola in hand. Alicia's three beloved dogs, Chili Weenie, Choco, and Little Girl, were her constant companions, providing her with comfort and happiness.

Alicia's life was one of profound connection and care."
